EDIT: I got it working, my goodness!

So, general MO2 etiquette calls for you not to click ‘unlock’ after an executable is running from MO2. Hence, I wasn’t doing that, and running the Launcher from the File Explorer, which was the issue. Once I clicked ‘unlock’ and ran the launcher from MO2–everything worked.

Sincere apologies for the confusion here: Nadeko, can you note this in your description by chance? Also, if you have the ability to, I would recommend creating a batch file to run both Server and Launcher at once, like the mod that this was inspired by. I don’t know if clicking unlock will create issues with SPT like it does with Skyrim, but maybe something to consider.

Thanks for your work! :)

Of course dude– this is working like a charm now.

Tldr: Run Server.exe Unlock MO2 Run Launcher.exe Play game

I was running the server, not unlocking, and running the launcher from MO2. Instead, I would run the launcher from file explorer, and while the server said it loaded, the launcher didn’t have access to the VFS.

On Archon’s old version, they state this: “When launching the game, you must use the option in the dropdown that looks like this: (no image) It makes sure both the server and the client can be ran at the same time and both have access to the VFS.”

Just some thoughts for you! It could be completely unfounded that unlocking while something is running messes with things, but I have zero knowledge of if that is true. Thanks for making this!

comments.author: Loneranger419
comments.body_html:
If you’re having weird issues with mods not loading or only partially loading, it’s often caused by an issue with the VFS that MO2 uses. It appears to be related to newer versions of Windows 11, and MO2 hasn’t been updated since 2024.

To fix it:

  • Download a release from usvfs GitHub.
  • Copy all of the files from the bin folder into the root of your MO2 installation, replacing the existing files if prompted.

I’ve personally had success using MO2 v2.5.2 with usvfs v0.5.7.2.

One more clarification after reading some of the comments: MO2 does not detect mods that are already installed. It can only manage mods that were installed through MO2.

If you want to convert a manually installed mod to an MO2-managed mod, first install the mod through MO2. Then, right-click the mod in MO2 and open its folder. Copy any configuration or data files you want to preserve into the MO2 version. Once you’ve confirmed everything was transferred correctly, back up and remove all remaining traces of the manually installed version from your SPT folder.

ALWAYS BACKUP YOUR PROFILES BEFORE LAUNCHING THE SERVER AFTER CHANGES
